title: Pick the composition to build
question: Three layouts in the Bench Analyzer world. Approve one, or name what to combine in the steer box (e.g. 'option 1 + the lamp matrix from 2'). Numbers in the images are placeholders; the build shows real pipeline output.

options.label: 1 · Circuit-first panel
options.thesis: The locked circuit on the graticule leads; controls on the right; channels and the REJECT lamp underneath.
options.viewport: Display 62% left, controls right, CH1-CH3 readouts and REJECT lamp below, statement strip at the bottom.
options.risk: The detection matrix and evidence live below the fold.

options.label: 2 · Dual-trace + lamp matrix
options.thesis: Your circuit vs what the compiler sees, stacked; the 5x3 lamp matrix and 1/4 vs 4/4 counters on the right.
options.viewport: Controls on a left rail, dual-trace center, lamp matrix right, channels and REJECT along the bottom.
options.risk: Densest of the three; everything competes on one screen.

options.label: 3 · Evidence-first
options.thesis: The proof leads: output histograms on a noisy copy of the device, a huge REJECT lamp and ESP readout, a ledger of recent runs.
options.viewport: Histogram display 66% left, REJECT lamp, ESP readout and channel rows right, run ledger at the bottom.
options.risk: The locked circuit shrinks to an inset, so 'the compiler sees nothing' is quieter.
